```{r, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Question 1: Fisher Randomization Tests

Reanalyze the experimental data using Fisher's randomization test (FRT) with
different test statistics. The null hypothesis is that the treatment has no
effect on any individual:

$$
H_0: \tau_i = 0, \quad \forall i = 1,2,\ldots,n.
$$

## Load and Prepare the Data

```{r}
lalonde <- read.table(
  "C:/Users/USER/Downloads/cps1re74.csv",
  header = TRUE
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    u74 = as.numeric(re74 == 0),
    u75 = as.numeric(re75 == 0)
  )

head(lalonde)
```

Define the number of observations and the number of treated individuals.

```{r}
n <- nrow(lalonde)
n1 <- sum(lalonde$treat == 1)

treat_permut <- function(n, n1) {
  A <- rep(0, n)
  A[sample(1:n, n1)] <- 1
  return(A)
}
```

## Approach I: Residual-Based Test Statistic

First, regress the outcome on all available covariates, excluding the treatment
variable, and obtain the residuals.

```{r}
model <- lm(re78 ~ . - treat, data = lalonde)
res <- model$residuals
```

Define the test statistic as the absolute difference between the mean residuals
of the treatment and comparison groups:

$$
T = \left|\overline{e}_1 - \overline{e}_0\right|,
$$

where $\overline{e}_1$ and $\overline{e}_0$ denote the mean residuals in the
treated and untreated groups, respectively.

```{r}
abs_res_diff <- function(A, res) {
  abs(mean(res[A == 1]) - mean(res[A == 0]))
}

I_0 <- abs_res_diff(lalonde$treat, res)

I_0
```

Generate random treatment assignments while keeping the number of treated
individuals fixed. Use these assignments to approximate the randomization
distribution under the null hypothesis.

```{r}
set.seed(007)

B <- 10000

I <- numeric(B)

for (i in 1:B) {
  comb <- treat_permut(n, n1)
  I[i] <- abs_res_diff(comb, res)
}

p_val_I <- mean(I >= I_0)

p_val_I
```

The Fisher randomization p-value is the proportion of permuted test statistics
that are at least as large as the observed statistic.

### Randomization Distribution

```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(I = I), aes(x = I)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 50,
    color = "black",
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = I_0,
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fisher Randomization Distribution: Approach I",
    x = "Absolute Difference in Mean Residuals",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Approach II: Treatment Coefficient as the Test Statistic

Fit a linear regression model of the outcome on treatment and all available
covariates. Use the estimated treatment coefficient as the observed test
statistic.

$$
\mathrm{re78}_i =
\beta_0 + \beta_1\mathrm{treat}_i
+ \sum_{j=2}^{p}\beta_j X_{ij} + \varepsilon_i,
$$

where $\beta_1$ is the treatment coefficient.

```{r}
model2 <- lm(re78 ~ ., data = lalonde)

coef_0 <- coef(model2)["treat"]

coef_0
```

Permute the treatment assignments while keeping the number of treated
individuals fixed, refit the regression model, and record the treatment
coefficient for each permutation.

```{r}
set.seed(007)

coef <- numeric(B)
data <- lalonde

for (i in 1:B) {
  data$treat <- treat_permut(n, n1)

  fit <- lm(re78 ~ ., data = data)

  coef[i] <- coef(fit)["treat"]
}

p_value_II <- mean(abs(coef) >= abs(coef_0))

p_value_II
```

The two-sided Fisher randomization p-value is

$$
p = \frac{1}{B}
\sum_{b=1}^{B}
\mathbf{1}\left(
|T_b| \geq |T_{\mathrm{obs}}|
\right),
$$

where $T_{\mathrm{obs}}$ is the observed treatment coefficient and $T_b$ is
the coefficient obtained from the $b$th permuted dataset.

### Randomization Distribution

```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(coef = coef), aes(x = coef)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 50,
    color = "black",
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = coef_0,
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fisher Randomization Distribution: Approach II",
    x = "Treatment Coefficient",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Approach III: Binary Outcome and Logistic Regression

Create a binary outcome that equals 1 when `re78` is positive and 0 otherwise.

```{r}
data <- lalonde |>
  mutate(bin78 = ifelse(re78 > 0, 1, 0))
```

Fit a logistic regression model of the binary outcome on treatment and the
covariates, excluding the original continuous outcome `re78`.

The model is

$$
\log\left(
\frac{P(\mathrm{bin78}_i=1)}
{1-P(\mathrm{bin78}_i=1)}
\right)
=
\beta_0 + \beta_1\mathrm{treat}_i
+ \sum_{j=2}^{p}\beta_j X_{ij}.
$$

```{r}
logit <- glm(
  bin78 ~ . - re78,
  data = data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

summary(logit)
```

The coefficient of `treat` represents the estimated change in log-odds of
having positive earnings in 1978, conditional on the other predictors. Its
statistical significance can be assessed using the coefficient's p-value in
the regression summary.

### Fisher Randomization Test for the Logistic Regression Coefficient

Use the treatment coefficient from the logistic regression as the test
statistic. Randomly permute the treatment assignments, refit the logistic
regression for each permutation, and calculate the two-sided randomization
p-value.

```{r}
set.seed(007)

B <- 2000

coef_0 <- coef(logit)["treat"]

coef <- numeric(B)

for (i in 1:B) {
  data$treat <- treat_permut(n, n1)

  fit <- glm(
    bin78 ~ . - re78,
    data = data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )

  coef[i] <- coef(fit)["treat"]
}

p_val_III <- mean(abs(coef) >= abs(coef_0))

p_val_III
```

### Randomization Distribution

```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(coef = coef), aes(x = coef)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = coef_0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fisher Randomization Distribution: Logistic Regression",
    x = "Treatment Coefficient",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
